entities.name_en: National Commissioner of the Icelandic Police

evidence.note: District police mailboxes on @logreglan.is listed on the official island.is government portal, e.g. nordurland.vestra@logreglan.is, vestfirdir@logreglan.is

entities.notes: Single national police; web presence migrated to island.is but email stays on logreglan.is.

entities.name_en: National Security Unit (analysis/intelligence unit of the National Police Commissioner)

evidence.note: Part of the National Commissioner of Police; shares the police mail domain

entities.notes: Iceland has no standalone intelligence agency; security intelligence/analysis is a police unit.
Maritime border/security body; also performs defence-related functions (air surveillance, Icelandic Defence Agency tasks absorbed 2011) as Iceland has no military.

entities.name_en: Ministry of Justice (interior-ministry equivalent: police, border, civil protection)

evidence.note: dmr@dmr.is listed as the ministry's email in the HCCH official authorities register; each Icelandic ministry has its own short mail domain

entities.notes: Website on the shared government portal stjornarradid.is; mail on dmr.is.

entities.name_en: Ministry for Foreign Affairs (Directorate for Defence — defence-ministry equivalent)

evidence.note: General address shown as utn[at]utn.is on the official ministry page

entities.notes: Iceland has no ministry of defence; defence and NATO affairs sit in the foreign ministry's defence directorate.

entities.name_en: National Computer Emergency Response Team of Iceland

evidence.note: cert@cert.is as team address (RFC 2350; also in Trusted Introducer directory PGP identity)

entities.notes: National CSIRT, hosted by the Electronic Communications Office (Fjarskiptastofa).

gaps: No military and no ministry of defence — defence functions covered by the Ministry for Foreign Affairs (policy) and the Coast Guard (operations); NATO membership without armed forces
No standalone intelligence agency — the National Security Unit of the National Police Commissioner covers security intelligence
Border control performed by the police (land/air) and Coast Guard (maritime); no separate border-guard agency
